member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Game.Map.MapView3D
member.summary:
The 3D map (14), replacing the flat inside the same shell (14 §9): real relief from the heightmap, satellite colour, the map mode as a fill per province, smooth borders, labels and picking. It works on the flat map's regions (US states and countries): every province of data/map/provinces.json names its region, so map modes, selection and the dossier are unchanged.
Terrain is a quadtree of one shared 64×64 patch mesh, lifted in the vertex shader (terrain.gdshader); patches split by distance to the camera and wrap east-west. The camera looks straight down from far away and tilts up to as it zooms in. Rasters load on a worker thread; until then the map shows the background.

member.name: T:SeatOfPower.Game.Map.Scatter
member.summary: Cities and forests on the 3D map (14 §8): 15's kit (D-034) placed from 13's urban layer (GHSL built-up share and mean height, LC100 forest density) near the camera, GPU-instanced with one per model. Placement is deterministic per L1 pixel (a hash of its position), cached per chunk of 64 × 64 L1 pixels, and only runs when zoomed in. Buildings are 9× their real footprint and trees 26× their real crown so they read at map scale; their height follows the terrain's exaggeration in the shaders. Ports (13's ports.json) get cranes and warehouses on the shore, more for bigger ports. The quality preset scales how many buildings and trees are placed and how far out. Each chunk gets a detail tier from how big a building or tree looks there (): the detailed mesh close in, the simple one beyond, and far forests thinned with wider crowns.

member.summary: The autoload that plays the game's sound (26 §4). It builds the buses (Master → Music, Ambience, Sfx, Ui; music ducks under game sounds), loads the cue table from data/audio/cues.json, and turns what happens into cues: button presses and panels (UI), simulation events, player commands and frame changes (, ), and the music's mood (). Everything that asks for a sound in one frame is a burst: of the UI cues and of the game cues, only the most important plays, within its cooldown ().

A game screen (11 §4), shown in a panel docked over the map (24 §2). The shell calls with each frame. Building Godot nodes is the expensive part of the UI (tens of microseconds a node), so a screen rebuilds its body only when what it lists changes: when differs from the last build, or after (a player action). Numbers move without a rebuild: , live charts () and re-read the frame themselves. A screen without rebuilds on a new day, at most every seconds while the game runs. Content lives in a scroll container that keeps its position across rebuilds.
A rebuild need not make every node again: parts made with stay while their own content is unchanged, and on a screen's first build, parts added with past are made on the next frames (the panel is still fading in).
